subject: general
question: Which of the following is an institutional source of credit in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Commercial bank.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Commercial bank:- **

 
 
• It is an institution that accepts deposit, makes business loans and offer related services to various like accepting deposits and lending loans and advances to general customers and business man.
 
• These institutions run to make profit.
 
• **Commercial banks is an institutional source of credit in India.**
 
• They cater to the financial requirements of industries and various sectors like agriculture, rural development, etc. it is a profit making institution owned by government or private of both.
 
• Commercial bank includes public sector, private sector, foreign banks and regional rural banks:
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Money lenders:-**

 
 
• Money lenders provide an alternative source of credit for individuals and small businesses who may have difficulty accessing loans from formal financial institutions like banks.
 
• This can help to bridge the gap between credit demand and supply.
 
 
 
• **Commission agents:-**
 
 
• Commission agents, also known as brokers or intermediaries, are individuals or firms that facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers in various markets.
 
• They play a significant role in economics by connecting buyers with sellers and helping to efficiently allocate resources.
 
 
 
• **Traders:-**
 
 
• These are individuals or entities that engage in the buying and selling of goods, services, or financial assets with the primary goal of generating profits.
 
• Traders play a significant role in economics and financial markets by facilitating the exchange of assets, contributing to market liquidity, and influencing price movements.
